summary: One session, two asks of one option: the first answered in full, as normal-with-greeks; then the gateway's link to IBKR drops, and the second ask's market data is accepted and never answered, behind a contract id the client already holds, so nothing is looked up again.

provenance.observed: 2026-11-08, during IBKR's Sunday maintenance (the market-data field notes of that day, the observation link-down is built on): the gateway's link to IBKR dropped while its own socket stayed open, isConnected stayed true, and every request was accepted and none answered. A client that already holds a session when the link drops, as the service always does, meets that silence on its NEXT ask, with every contract id it resolved before the drop still cached.
provenance.why: The link cannot be dropped on demand, still less between two asks of one session, and that session's bytes were not kept. link-down cannot stand in for it: there every lookup is fresh, so the silence is met at the lookup, where here nothing is looked up again and the silence is met only at the market data, behind a cached contract id.
provenance.built: normal-with-greeks (recorded 2026-11-09), whole: its greeting, session messages, lookup and market-data exchange, which answer the first ask. Then ONE addition: a second reqMktData exchange for the same contract, its sent fields copied from the first, with no reply, which answers the second ask by the turn rule (README, rule 3). That silence is the only thing invented. The 2110, 2103 and 2157 notices that announced the drop on 2026-11-08 are not here: the format has no place for a message sent unasked between two asks, and IbkrClient routes nothing sent against request id -1 to a request (link-down carries them, at the session's start).
